target_customer: Software developers and teams running coding agents in parallel
problem: Running several dev environments or agent worktrees in parallel overloads laptops and collides on ports.
business_model: Developer tool / cloud runtime, hosted or bring-your-own-cloud (pricing not found)

founders.name: Jeffrey Lin
education: University of Waterloo, Systems Design Engineering
previous_startups: Two prior startups, two exits per YC page

technical_complexity.rationale: Provisioning isolated cloud machines, networking and port forwarding behind a CLI is standard infrastructure engineering with some hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Cloud dev environments are a crowded category and CLI wrappers are easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early to observe; batch is Winter 2027.

market_need_then: Parallel coding agents increase local resource contention; no dated demand evidence beyond the founders' pitch was found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Page is written partly as setup guide for AI agents

brand_strength.rationale: No brand sources. Name resembles other products (Tessl, Tesseract, Tessera in search results), a mild confusability risk.

outcome_analysis: Tesser is a Winter 2027 company, so no outcome exists. It sells a CLI that moves dev servers, builds and tests to isolated cloud machines. The founders have startup and developer-tool experience, but the category is crowded and no traction or funding is public.
notes: Batch is in the future relative to the research date (2026-11); the YC page lists W27. Competitors left empty: nothing dated near the batch was found. takeover_risk incumbents are my category judgment, not sourced. Searches returned nothing beyond YC page, site and one directory listing.
